segments.name: Franchise & Base Management Fees
segments.description: Fees from franchised and managed properties, including base management fees and franchise fees. Core high-margin revenue stream.
segments.notes: Driven by rooms growth, RevPAR increases, and higher co-branded credit card fees. Fee revenue grew 8% in FY2025 ($716M incremental).

segments.name: Incentive Management Fees
segments.description: Performance-based fees from managed hotels, tied to property profitability.
segments.notes: International markets contributed ~2/3 of incentive fees in Q4 2025. Luxury segment outperformance drives higher incentive fee capture.

segments.name: Owned, Leased & Other Revenue
segments.description: Revenue from properties Marriott directly owns or leases. Minimal and declining as asset-light strategy continues.
segments.notes: Negligible contribution to overall revenue mix; Marriott is systematically divesting owned properties.

segments.name: Cost Reimbursements
segments.description: Pass-through revenues that offset reimbursed expenses from managed and franchised properties.
segments.notes: Low/zero margin pass-through. Represents ~74% of reported revenue but not a meaningful earnings driver.

geographic_breakdown.revpar_trend_2025: Roughly flat; impacted by government shutdown and softer select-service/extended-stay demand
geographic_breakdown.notes: Dominant region. RevPAR flat in 2025 due to government shutdown impact on business transient.

geographic_breakdown.revpar_trend_2025: International RevPAR +6% led by EMEA and APEC; APAC +9%, EMEA +7%
geographic_breakdown.notes: FY2024 revenue decline partly due to reporting reclassification of 'Unallocated Corporate' ($1.56B in FY2023 moved). International RevPAR strong in 2025.
Reported as sub-segment of International. Separate RevPAR tracking. Recovery trajectory post-COVID but lagging EMEA/APAC.

supply_chain.business_model: Asset-light, fee-driven. ~75% franchised, ~25% managed. Minimal owned/leased properties.
supply_chain.gross_margin_vs_hilton: ~20% higher than Hilton due to management-heavy model
key_partnerships: Co-branded credit cards (fee revenue growing, +33% expected in 2026 from new card launches)
Bonvoy loyalty platform (228M+ members in 2024, 270M+ by end 2025, +43M added in 2025)

tam.notes: TAM growing but mature markets face supply constraints from high interest rates. Asia-Pacific and Middle East driving pipeline growth.

loyalty_program.name: Marriott Bonvoy
loyalty_program.strategic_role: Core direct booking channel; co-branded credit cards major fee revenue driver
